compliance_report.summary: Verified all 17 stakeholder and domain-derived requirements against the Indian banking and data protection knowledge base. All checks are supported by retrieved regulatory/security evidence.

checks.requirement: Customers shall be able to open fixed/recurring deposits and view loan amortization schedules. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Digital banking services must provide transparent, accurate financial disclosures and protect transaction integrity across customer-facing channels (rbi_digital_payment_security_directions_2026.txt, owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt).
checks.notes: Supported by deterministic financial calculation validation and secure customer portal access.

checks.requirement: Customers shall be able to apply for personal or home loans and download tax/interest certificates. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Customer onboarding for credit facilities requires verified Customer Due Diligence (CDD) records (rbi_kyc_directions_2025.txt), and access to personal financial summaries requires strict object-level authorization (owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt).
checks.notes: Aligned with digital credit onboarding and authenticated document retrieval controls.

checks.requirement: Customers shall be able to submit data privacy (consent withdrawal/erasure) or grievance requests. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Data Fiduciaries must provide Data Principals with an easily accessible mechanism to withdraw consent, request data erasure/correction, and register grievances within prescribed timelines (dpdp_act_2023.txt, dpdp_rules_2025.txt).
checks.notes: Directly mandated by statutory Data Principal rights and grievance redressal rules.

checks.requirement: Loan underwriters and branch managers shall be able to verify customer KYC documents and evaluate credit eligibility. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Regulated Entities must verify customer identity using Officially Valid Documents (OVDs) or digital KYC/V-CIP workflows and maintain periodic KYC updation records (rbi_kyc_directions_2025.txt).
checks.notes: Supported by KYC verification and credit underwriting governance standards.

checks.requirement: Loan underwriters and branch managers shall be able to approve or reject loan applications using maker-checker workflows. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Financial applications must enforce separation of duties and dual-authorization controls for high-value financial approvals (owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt, nist_csf_2_0.txt).
checks.notes: Prevents unilateral loan approval fraud through enforced maker-checker state transitions.

checks.requirement: Loan underwriters and branch managers shall be able to freeze accounts flagged for suspicious activity. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Regulated Entities must monitor suspicious transactions under AML/CFT obligations (rbi_kyc_directions_2025.txt) and maintain rapid incident containment capabilities (nist_csf_2_0.txt).
checks.notes: Supported by AML/CFT enforcement and operational containment controls.

checks.requirement: Bank administrators and compliance officers shall be able to configure interest rate slabs and define user roles and access permissions. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Access control standards require Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), least-privilege enforcement, and strict governance over privileged administrative actions (owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt, nist_csf_2_0.txt).
checks.notes: Supported by RBAC and administrative configuration governance.

checks.requirement: Bank administrators and compliance officers shall be able to generate statutory regulatory reports and inspect immutable system audit logs. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Regulated Entities must maintain auditable KYC/transaction records (rbi_kyc_directions_2025.txt), retain ICT logs securely for 180 days within India with NTP-synchronized clocks (cert_in_directions_2022.txt), and preserve tamper-evident processing logs (dpdp_rules_2025.txt).
checks.notes: Directly supported by statutory log retention, clock synchronization, and auditability mandates.

checks.requirement: The system shall prevent duplicate loan disbursements and ensure accurate interest and EMI calculations. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Application business logic must enforce idempotency, atomic transaction processing, and protection against race conditions or replay attacks (owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt).
checks.notes: Supported by transactional integrity and deterministic financial validation controls.

checks.requirement: The system shall enforce consent management and statutory data retention/erasure controls. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Personal data must only be processed for specified consented purposes and erased once the purpose is fulfilled, subject to overriding statutory banking retention laws (dpdp_act_2023.txt, dpdp_rules_2025.txt, rbi_kyc_directions_2025.txt).
checks.notes: Balances DPDP erasure mandates with mandatory RBI KYC/financial record retention periods.

checks.requirement: The system shall restrict access to customer financial records to authorized personnel only. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Data Fiduciaries must implement technical safeguards including encryption, access controls, and masking to prevent unauthorized personal data access (dpdp_act_2023.txt, dpdp_rules_2025.txt, owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt).
checks.notes: Supported by confidentiality and authorization enforcement standards.

checks.requirement: The system shall provide a clear, accessible user interface. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Consent notices and customer interfaces must be clear, itemized, and understandable (dpdp_act_2023.txt, dpdp_rules_2025.txt), supporting transparent customer interactions (rbi_digital_payment_security_directions_2026.txt).
checks.notes: Aligned with transparent notice and usability guidelines.

checks.requirement: The system shall safeguard confidential customer information in compliance with Indian banking and data protection laws. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Systems must implement reasonable security safeguards, strong cryptography in transit and at rest, and breach notification readiness (dpdp_act_2023.txt, dpdp_rules_2025.txt, cert_in_directions_2022.txt, rbi_digital_payment_security_directions_2026.txt).
checks.notes: Fully supported by statutory privacy, security, and breach-reporting mandates.

checks.requirement: The system shall support multiple concurrent users simultaneously. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Critical banking infrastructure must ensure operational availability, resilience, and concurrency safety (rbi_digital_payment_security_directions_2026.txt, nist_csf_2_0.txt).
checks.notes: Aligned with availability and concurrency resilience standards.

checks.requirement: The system shall ensure reliable, tamper-evident storage of financial records. (Explicit)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Systems must maintain data integrity, verifiable backups, and immutable audit trails (dpdp_rules_2025.txt, owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt, nist_csf_2_0.txt).
checks.notes: Supported by data integrity and forensic logging requirements.

checks.requirement: The system shall implement privacy-by-design, strong authentication, and cryptographic security controls by default. (Domain-derived)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: Security and privacy controls must be embedded into architecture by design, including MFA, session security, and cryptographic key management (dpdp_act_2023.txt, rbi_digital_payment_security_directions_2026.txt, owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt).
checks.notes: Mandated by privacy-by-design and application security verification baselines.

checks.requirement: The system shall maintain synchronized system clocks, forensic audit logs, and deterministic calculation traceability across all financial operations. (Domain-derived)
checks.standard: Indian banking and data protection knowledge base
checks.evidence: ICT systems must synchronize clocks to NTP/NPL servers and maintain tamper-proof logs for forensic auditing (cert_in_directions_2022.txt, owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt).
checks.notes: Supported by forensic readiness and regulatory audit standards.

factors_considered.evidence: Core accounting formulas, loan amortization logic, maker-checker rules, and statutory reporting formats are well-defined upfront.
Regulatory mandates and core banking workflows are deterministic and standardized.
Standard enterprise banking architecture with well-established transactional database and integration patterns.
High risk due to direct financial exposure, loan disbursement errors, and severe statutory non-compliance penalties.
High financial criticality; rounding errors, race conditions, or unauthorized disbursements directly impact customer funds and bank solvency.

factors_considered.assessment_level: Derived from retrieved Indian banking and data protection knowledge
factors_considered.evidence: RBI Master Directions, DPDP Act/Rules, CERT-In Directions, OWASP ASVS, and NIST CSF apply.
Internal banking workflows and regulatory reports follow fixed compliance specifications rather than exploratory UX.
Business rules and statutory formulas are deterministic and require formal verification rather than exploratory prototyping.
Integrates with core accounting ledgers, credit bureaus, KYC registries, and regulatory reporting gateways.

supporting_evidence: High requirement stability (loan amortization math, maker-checker rules, KYC checks, and regulatory reports are fixed upfront)
High financial criticality requiring deterministic verification of interest, EMI, and ledger balances
Strict regulatory compliance (rbi_kyc_directions_2025.txt, rbi_digital_payment_security_directions_2026.txt, dpdp_act_2023.txt, dpdp_rules_2025.txt, cert_in_directions_2022.txt)
Need for formal bidirectional traceability between statutory rules, security controls (owasp_asvs_5_0_0.txt, nist_csf_2_0.txt), and test protocols
Multi-role governance requiring rigorous validation of RBAC and maker-checker approval boundaries
Low need for exploratory prototyping due to standardized banking domain rules
sdlc_recommendation.explanation: Developing a core banking ledger, loan origination, and statutory reporting system involves strict regulatory compliance (RBI, DPDP, CERT-In), deterministic financial mathematics, and zero tolerance for calculation or disbursement errors. Because the banking rules, interest/EMI formulas, maker-checker workflows, and statutory reporting schemas are well-defined and stable upfront, the V-Model is the ideal SDLC choice. It pairs every specification and architectural design phase on the left side of the V with a formal verification and validation phase on the right side—ensuring complete bidirectional traceability from regulatory mandates and financial formulas down to unit tests, integration tests, security penetration testing (OWASP ASVS), and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) prior to production release.
sdlc_recommendation.tie_break_notes: V-Model is preferred over Waterfall because verification and validation are explicitly required for deterministic financial and regulatory controls.
